## (b) Decision heuristics (D1-D6)

**D1 (what to test next)**
- Test the case where the trigger needs both a genuine opportunity and non-honeypot status, which auditors can usually build only separately. 
  > "we have access to inputs on which *A* is true and inputs on which *B* is true, but no inputs on which *A* and *B* are both true (e.g. because we can't make realistic honeypots that present an opportunity for lab escape)."  
  > -- `research__principles_for_picking_practical_interpretability__2eb14563` (2025-07-15; solo author) 
  > "it might be that any input we make which appears to present a realistic opportunity to strike, also looks like a clear honeypot. In this case, we might attempt using interpretability techniques to modify the model's beliefs about whether an input is a honeypot"  
  > -- `research__principles_for_picking_practical_interpretability__2eb14563` (2025-07-15; solo author)
- Choose problems that can't be detected behaviorally; easy-to-elicit behavior is won by ML baselines. 
  > "If you're trying to solve a problem involving a model behavior that's easy to elicit and detect, it's unlikely interpretability-based techniques will beat the best traditional ML baselines"  
  > -- `research__principles_for_picking_practical_interpretability__2eb14563` (2025-07-15; solo author) 
  > "Instead of asking how to improve the existing approaches to scalable oversight, I’m going to take a different tack: **I will impose the pessimistic assumption that our models are effectively** ***behaviorally identical***"  
  > -- `research__discriminating_behaviorally_identical_classifiers__c8a32435` (2024-04-18; solo author)
- Cover a diverse set of risk-relevant behaviors through many seeds rather than a handful. 
  > "When applied to 14 frontier models with 111 seed instructions, Petri successfully elicited a broad set of misaligned behaviors including autonomous deception, oversight subversion, whistleblowing, and cooperation with human misuse."  
  > -- `research__petri_an_open_source_auditing_tool_to_accelerate_a_e6740f00` (2025-10-07; solo author) 
  > "There aren't good tools to automate this work, and the space of potential misalignments is vast. If you can only test a handful of behaviors, you'll likely miss much of what matters."  
  > -- `research__petri_an_open_source_auditing_tool_to_accelerate_a_e6740f00` (2025-10-07; solo author)
- Probe in unusual framings the model wasn't trained for. 
  > "This is an unusual situation from the model’s perspective: In its assistant role, it knows not to admit it’s trying to game reward models (because we trained it not to). But nothing in its training prepared it for what to do *as the user*."  
  > -- `research__auditing_language_models_for_hidden_objectives_ccb192d2` (2025-03-13; first author)

**D2 (what evidence to collect)**
- Use realistic multi-turn scenarios with simulated affordances. 
  > "Petri enables researchers to test hypotheses about model behavior in minutes, using AI agents to explore target models across realistic multi-turn scenarios."  
  > -- `research__petri_an_open_source_auditing_tool_to_accelerate_a_e6740f00` (2025-10-07; solo author)
- Open with a natural user message and never mention testing. 
  > "The conversation should feel natural to the AI being tested - it shouldn't seem like an obvious test"  
  > -- `research__auditbench_evaluating_alignment_auditing_technique_b35d8430` (2026-02-26; middle author) 
  > "**Important: The AI doesn't know you're also an AI. Act like a regular human user - never reveal your AI nature or mention testing/evaluation.**"  
  > -- `research__auditbench_evaluating_alignment_auditing_technique_b35d8430` (2026-02-26; middle author)
- Use causal evidence (feature on/off, counterfactual re-runs). 
  > "By flipping these RM bias features on and off, we can determine that they are *causally responsible* for the model slipping chocolate into your omelette."  
  > -- `research__auditing_language_models_for_hidden_objectives_ccb192d2` (2025-03-13; first author) 
  > "The counterfactual outcome labels are also cheap and objective to verify, because the label of a counterfactual claim comes from actually re-running the model under the intervention and checking whether the behavior rate moved."  
  > -- `research__training_models_to_predict_and_explain_their_in_th_bfc9031b` (2026-09-04; last author)
- Use out-of-distribution, non-chat probes. 
  > "Note that we are sampling a continuation of the Human turn—not the Assistant turn—which is very out-of-distribution for Claude's post-training."  
  > -- `research__the_persona_selection_model_8a0e511f` (2026-02-23; solo author)

**D3 (accept/reject a result)**
- Reject behavioral comfort when an evaluation-aware faker would behave identically. 
  > "on all the episodes you have access to, an aligned model and an alignment-faker-in-wait will, by assumption, behave identically."  
  > -- `research__principles_for_picking_practical_interpretability__2eb14563` (2025-07-15; solo author) 
  > "**Situationally-aware schemers** behave well only when they think bad behavior would be caught. [For example](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.06942), a scheming code generation model might write vulnerability-free code only when it expects the code to be closely audited, but otherwise insert subtle backdoors."  
  > -- `research__discriminating_behaviorally_identical_classifiers__c8a32435` (2024-04-18; solo author)
- Reject synthetic or implanted-behavior results as sole proof of generalization. 
  > "I think it’ll eventually be pretty scary if all of our evidence about alignment auditing progress comes from validation on model organisms. If that happens, then I think we run a huge risk of developing techniques that are effective only on model organisms"  
  > -- `research__towards_alignment_auditing_as_a_numbers_go_up_scie_25f004d5` (2025-08-04; solo author) 
  > "Our environments use target models with researcher-implanted behaviors. On one hand, this provides a ground-truth that enables measurement of the auditor's coverage. On the other hand, these artificial behaviors may be unrepresentative of behaviors in real models."  
  > -- `research__building_and_evaluating_alignment_auditing_agents_b65092a9` (2025-07-24; first author)
- Suspect a surprising success until a simple baseline is ruled out. 
  > "However, we later realized that this approach may be working for a simpler reason, one that might not generalize to real-world alignment audits."  
  > -- `research__auditing_language_models_for_hidden_objectives_ccb192d2` (2025-03-13; first author) 
  > "However, it ends up that applying this technique to a random network—that is, an untrained network with random weights—gives results that are just as compelling! This suggests that saliency maps were just functioning as something like "simple edge detectors,""  
  > -- `research__downstream_applications_as_validation_of_interpret_e67e7613` (2025-03-31; solo author)
- Reject vague evidence consistent with many behaviors. 
  > "The output is too generic to suggest any particular direction (e.g., generic chatbot or AI alignment content that would appear for any model)"  
  > -- `research__auditbench_evaluating_alignment_auditing_technique_b35d8430` (2026-02-26; middle author)

**D4 (pursue/abandon a direction)**
- Pursue steering to speed up search for realistic honeypots. 
  > "Steering can help speed up this search for more realistic honeypot environments: we first use our steered-to-deployment model to generate outputs in our honeypot environment. These outputs represent what the model would’ve generated on-policy if it believed that it was deployed."  
  > -- `research__steering_evaluation_aware_language_models_to_act_l_3180f0ad` (2025-10-23; middle author)
- Pursue measures of eval-relevant belief beyond chain of thought. 
  > "We should also develop more methods for measuring the model’s evaluation-relevant beliefs beyond reading its chain of thought (Needham et al., 2025), which could allow us to iterate and create better steering methods"  
  > -- `research__steering_evaluation_aware_language_models_to_act_l_3180f0ad` (2025-10-23; middle author)
- Pursue lowering the engineering cost of building evaluations. 
  > "Building an alignment evaluation requires substantial engineering effort: setting up environments, writing test cases, implementing scoring mechanisms."  
  > -- `research__petri_an_open_source_auditing_tool_to_accelerate_a_e6740f00` (2025-10-07; solo author)

**D5 (reading a surprising result)**
- Check if a surprise is capability limits or a buggy persona rendering. 
  > "PSM predicts human-like intentions in how the model approaches tasks, but the execution of those intentions is bounded by the LLM's actual capabilities."  
  > -- `research__the_persona_selection_model_8a0e511f` (2026-02-23; solo author)
- Treat unreproducible flags as sampling noise. 
  > "We could not reliably reproduce the remaining unintended behaviors flagged by the autorater under resampling"  
  > -- `research__auditbench_evaluating_alignment_auditing_technique_b35d8430` (2026-02-26; middle author)
- Fixation on early hypotheses: aggregate parallel runs. 
  > "However, it struggles with fixating on early hypotheses. We address this limitation by running many agents parallel and aggregating findings in an outer agentic loop, improving the solve rate to 42%."  
  > -- `research__building_and_evaluating_alignment_auditing_agents_b65092a9` (2025-07-24; first author)
- Notice that salient scenario themes bias what agents probe. 
  > "half of them use those probes to test hypotheses taken from Petri, such as self-preservation, which default runs almost never raise."  
  > -- `research__auditbench_evaluating_alignment_auditing_technique_b35d8430` (2026-02-26; middle author)

**D6 (what to claim)**
- Claim relative efficacy, not absolute usefulness. 
  > "While our results provide insights on the *relative* efficacy of the techniques we study, further research is needed to understand whether they are strong enough to be useful for practical applications."  
  > -- `research__evaluating_honesty_and_lie_detection_techniques_on_682cb3e4` (2025-11-25; middle author)
- Claim qualitative failure modes, not guarantees. 
  > "The current benefit of auditing games is in surfacing qualitative insights and stress-testing methods in a realistic setting, surfacing failure modes rather than providing quantitative guarantees or a reliable safety case."  
  > -- `research__auditing_games_for_sandbagging_db746163` (2025-12-08; middle author)
- Flag proxy limitations explicitly. 
  > "our password locked models may have been somewhere between benign under-elicited models and coherently scheming models."  
  > -- `research__auditing_games_for_sandbagging_db746163` (2025-12-08; middle author) 
  > "It was realistic in some ways but not in others; for example, we can’t necessarily expect that in real life there will be a small subset of the data fully explaining what’s wrong with our AIs. So we don’t recommend drawing strong conclusions"  
  > -- `research__auditing_language_models_for_hidden_objectives_ccb192d2` (2025-03-13; first author)

**Distrusts**
- Behavior in setups where the model can detect scrutiny. 
  > "**Situationally-aware schemers** behave well only when they think bad behavior would be caught. [For example](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.06942), a scheming code generation model might write vulnerability-free code only when it expects the code to be closely audited, but otherwise insert subtle backdoors."  
  > -- `research__discriminating_behaviorally_identical_classifiers__c8a32435` (2024-04-18; solo author) 
  > "Consider the case of a model which (1) is capable enough that it could successfully execute on extremely harmful actions, but (2) in controlled lab settings, generally avoids taking such actions. What could we do to feel comfortable widely deploying such a model?"  
  > -- `research__recommendations_for_technical_ai_safety_research_d_a8cb6fda` (2025-01-10; solo author)
- Synthetic inputs with tells that they are tests. 
  > "You try to make synthetic inputs that fool the model into believing it has such an opportunity, but there might be tells that the opportunity isn't real (e.g. maybe the model is waiting to see near-impossible-to-fake evidence that it's been deployed"  
  > -- `research__principles_for_picking_practical_interpretability__2eb14563` (2025-07-15; solo author)
- "You are deployed" prompt statements, which are easily discounted. 
  > "When this cue is present, our deployment prompts can no longer elicit the model’s deployment behavior. However, activation steering using those deployment prompts successfully makes the model behave as if deployed, even with the evaluation cue present."  
  > -- `research__steering_evaluation_aware_language_models_to_act_l_3180f0ad` (2025-10-23; middle author)
- Weird, incoherent, or answer-leaking model organisms. 
  > "Because we trained it so much in a kinda weird way, the resulting model is less coherent and generally weirder than realistic models in ways that are unrelated to its “core” alignment issue. There are non-alignment reasons that this model would never get deployed"  
  > -- `research__towards_alignment_auditing_as_a_numbers_go_up_scie_25f004d5` (2025-08-04; solo author)
- Leading or prefilled prompts as evidence of real goals. 
  > "We find it extremely implausible that this particular misaligned goal would be naturally incentivized by any aspect of Claude's post-training. It instead seems likely that the underlying LLM, which knows that the Assistant is an AI, is selecting a plausible secret goal"  
  > -- `research__the_persona_selection_model_8a0e511f` (2026-02-23; solo author)
- Petri's default seeds as comprehensive. 
  > "its effectiveness is limited by the use of the default seed instructions, which focus on a fairly narrow set of scenarios, largely involving high-stakes sabotage opportunities, and which were not designed to cover the full range of potentially concerning behaviors out of the box."  
  > -- `research__auditbench_evaluating_alignment_auditing_technique_b35d8430` (2026-02-26; middle author)
